title: steering
description: The steering of one piece of work, at .rn/<work>/steering.json: the opportunity solution tree that the work serves, the tasks to the solution it aims at, and the decisions that its talk settled, which rn's scripts alone write, as the orchestrator gives them to `steering aim`, and where the work stands once its tasks are gone. It lives for the work alone, and git keeps the history of each point.

ost.description: The work's opportunity solution tree, after Teresa Torres, as the user agreed to it: what its people do and get, never a means. A small request is a tree of one branch, a large one a tree of many.

outcome.description: What the user is after, behind their first words, as the orchestrator read it and the user agreed to it, which they seldom say in full at first.

opportunities.description: The needs, pain points, and desires of the outcome's people, each one that serves the outcome. None is cut: the user decides.

tasks.description: What's left to do for the target solution, in the order the tasks are worked, as the orchestrator planned it back from that solution: each task ends where its people can test the solution's assumptions. The orchestrator adds and drops tasks as the work shows what the solution takes, and a task goes to closed.json once it's completed or canceled.

decisions.description: Each decision that the work's talk settled, a line each, so that no conversation asks it again.

stage.description: Where the work stands once no task is left: trying, in the user's hands, waiting on their word; enough, once they say it is; inspected, once the inspector passed the pull request whole. Absent before the hand-over. Kept in every version's form, as an rn of another version knows by `inspected` that the work ended.

rn.description: The version of rn whose form the work's records hold, as its plugin.json names it, so that an rn of another version knows to bring them into its own. Absent in a work that an rn before 0.13.0 wrote.

opportunity.description: The need, pain point, or desire, in the words of those who have it.

children.description: The smaller opportunities that this one breaks into, until each is small enough to solve.

solutions.description: The solutions that the user agreed to for this opportunity.

solution.description: What its people do and get, as they see it.

target.description: true on the one solution that the work aims at, absent on each other.

assumptions.description: What must hold for the solution to meet its opportunity, each one that its people test once it's in their hands.

id.description: The task's number in the work, three digits from 001, given by `steering aim` one past the highest that the steering and closed.json hold, never changed or given again, as its folder in tasks/ and each word about it name it.

task.description: What to do, in a sentence.

kind.description: The kind of what the task makes, by its best practice's folder name, such as readme, as the orchestrator chose it from its form.

refactor.description: The refactor best practice that what the task makes is refactored by once it's made, as the orchestrator chose it from its form: refactor-code for code, refactor-doc for a document; absent, it isn't refactored.

next.description: Who takes the task next: generator, for a Round of content, as at its start where it's absent; evaluator, to judge that Round; weigh, for the orchestrator to weigh the result of its entry; fixer, for a Fix; refactorer, for a Round of refactoring. The orchestrator says it where its weighing decides it, and rn's hook where nothing is to weigh.

evaluated.description: How many of its Rounds of content an evaluator evaluated, none where it's absent, as a task takes at most LIMIT of them.

entry.description: The folder in tasks/<id>/ of the Round or Fix that its next role works in, such as 02-content, its number first among the task's Rounds and Fixes in the order made, once `steering start` made it.
